summary.text: A 59-year-old Japanese man with hepatitis B infection at 24 years of age was well until 3 weeks before admission and one week before admission visited a local hospital with fever and watery diarrhea; broad-spectrum antibiotics did not help and workup found no cause. He was transferred with fever, ascites and pleural effusion; on admission he had fever, abdominal distension, pitting leg edema, leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, hypoalbuminemia and raised CRP, IL-6 and VEGF.

CT showed ascites, bilateral pleural and pericardial effusion and mild bilateral renal hypertrophy without other organomegaly or lymphadenopathy. Cultures, tumor markers, HHV-8, HIV, Rickettsia, Aspergillus and tuberculosis tests were negative. Bone marrow biopsy showed increased megakaryocytes with mild reticulin fibrosis; right inguinal lymph node biopsy showed Castleman-like features without monoclonal plasma cells, compatible with mixed-type Castleman disease and TAFRO syndrome.

Despite meropenem, vancomycin, doxycycline and diuretics, fever and anasarca worsened. Methylprednisolone was given on day 10 and prednisolone started on day 13. On day 17 he developed respiratory distress and circulatory failure and went into pulseless electrical activity in the general ward. After resuscitation he was hypotensive in intensive care, needing frequent adrenaline, and blood pressure was maintained by draining 4,000 mL of ascites, after which left ventricular contraction became normokinetic; drainage continued for 6 weeks.

TAFRO syndrome was diagnosed on day 18 and tocilizumab was initiated. Some inflammatory parameters improved for 5 days after tocilizumab, but the anasarca worsened, so cyclosporin A was given from day 24 along with prednisolone and tocilizumab. Symptoms and laboratory data gradually improved over 3 months, and he was discharged home on day 112.
